_comment: Where each bundled artifact came from, so `gameversion.status()` can say
whether it still matches the installed game. Regenerate an entry's
`gameBuild` whenever you re-run its script against a new install.
A null `gameBuild` means the origin build is genuinely unknown, not that it
is current. `gameversion` reports that as 'unknown' rather than assuming a
match, because a wrong-but-plausible map is worse than an honest banner.

Build 24466863 (installed 2026-08-04) shipped NO server-pak change - Pal-LinuxServer.pak is byte-identical to 24370498's, and check-game-build --extract re-derived all 13 world-object categories (59,396 objects) with zero differences. Server-pak-only artifacts therefore carry 24466863; mixed-source artifacts (client pak L10N, PalWorldSaveTools archive, docs site) keep their extraction-time stamp, because only their server-pak half is verified unchanged.

Build 24575149 (v1.0.3, public 2026-08-12; id from the SteamCMD API public branch) - the operator supplied its Pal-LinuxServer.pak on 2026-08-17 and every server-pak artifact was RE-DERIVED against it: 6 changed (economy, raidbosses, game_settings, settings_help, gamedata, worldobjects[gzip-canonicalised only]), the rest byte-identical. World-object positions: 59,396 of 59,396 unchanged. Client-pak artifacts (lang/, guild, icons) keep their stamps - Pal-Windows.pak has not been updated, so v1.0.3's new/changed strings are not in the language packs yet.

achievements.json.gz.note: The game's own milestone NPC — 26 rows in three categories (PalCapture 10 tiers 100-1000, PalDex 10 tiers 10-100, BossDefeat 6 tiers 5-100), each with a reward item and an EXP bonus level. POCKETPAIR'S TYPO IS KEPT: the DataTable and the save key are both `Achivement`, and correcting it breaks the join. THESE ARE NOT STEAM ACHIEVEMENTS — Steam's need GetPlayerAchievements, a publisher key and each player's SteamID, i.e. a runtime dependency on an external API this project forbids, and they would be per-account rather than per-server. CLAIMED IS A JOIN, NOT AN INFERENCE: RecordData.NPCAchivementRewardFlag names the row outright (`PalDex_7`) and 26 of 26 claimed keys across refworld's five players resolve to a row here. Only the PROGRESS BAR needs a counter, and BossDefeat ships `counter: null` because none is established — no BossDefeatCount exists, TowerBossDefeatFlag maxes at 7 observed against a top tier of 100 so it cannot be towers alone, and the claim data cannot separate field-only from field-plus-tower since every player who claimed the 5-boss tier clears it either way. PalDex maps to TribeCaptureCount, which READ AS 0 FOR EVERY PLAYER until 2026-08-12 because it is a plain int and the parser treated it as a map; real values are 210/149/128/109/8. The mapping's validation is that no player has CLAIMED a tier their counter has not reached, checked across all five.

basecamp.json.gz.note: 35 base levels with the worker cap (1-30) and bases-per-guild cap (up to 4), 8 illnesses with their real work-speed, move-speed and satiety penalties plus the hourly palbox cure chance, and 11 worker events with the sanity each triggers at. THE LEVEL TABLE IS A DEFAULT, NOT A BOUND, and that is measured: a real server in use runs 5 bases per guild and 25 workers, over the table in one direction and under it in the other. BaseCampWorkerMaxNum, BaseCampMaxNumInGuild and BaseCampMaxNum are all PalWorldSettings.ini keys, so the INI is the only authority and gamedata.server_limit() reads it; None means not known, never unlimited and never 'use the game's value'. Base level is not in the save at all (BaseCampSaveData carries id, name, state, transform, area_range, group and the owning palbox, and the palbox carries no level either), so the per-level table currently has no caller. Illness detail: DisturbingElement is -50%/-50% at only 3%/hr palbox cure; Cold is -5% at 20%/hr — so 'sick' can stop being a flag. The sanity thresholds matter separately: a worker takes short breaks at 85 and has stopped being useful well before main.LOW_SANITY's 50, which comes from FriendshipPoint_AutoIncrementRequireSanity and measures trust gain rather than misbehaviour. Read verification: the table's top worker cap of 30 must be >= the 25-slot worker container observed on the live world. Debug_DisplayName is Pocketpair's internal Japanese label, flagged debugNameIsInternal so nothing renders it. Condition display names come from the client pak because the server table carries only an internal SickType and the event table's debugName is Japanese. `Cold` displays as "Sick" — the id and the player-facing name genuinely disagree, which is why they are looked up rather than humanised. Without the client pak the bundle still builds and `nameIsInternal` is true.
basecamp.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak DT_BaseCampLevelData / DT_BaseCampWorkerSickDataTable / DT_BaseCampWorkerEventDataTable; condition NAMES and descriptions from Pal-Windows.pak L10N/en DT_UI_Common_Text_Common

boss_spawners.json.gz.note: 90 placed field bosses with species, LEVEL and world position — levels 11-79, 89 distinct species. The table has 159 rows; 69 are unused spawner slots and are not bosses. Positions verified against the World Partition cell grid: 90/90 land on an occupied MainGrid_L0 cell at 25,600 units, with controls at 12,800 (22/90) and 51,200 (83/90) both worse, which is what makes it evidence. Contains no RAID_ ids and should not: raid bosses are altar-summoned, not world-placed.

build_capabilities.json.gz.note: What a STRUCTURE contributes to base output. 48 structures: WorkSpeedAdditionalRate on 33 (BlastFurnace 1.0 -> BlastFurnace2 1.5 -> BlastFurnace3 3.0 -> BlastFurnace4 4.5 -> AncientBlastFurnace 11.0), ReviveSpeedMultiplier on 6 medical beds, GenerateEnergyRateByWorker on 4 (hand-cranked 0.2 -> Ancient 20.0), AffectSanityRate on 4 including the Spa, MaxEnergyStorage on 1. FOUND BY CLASS, NOT BY NAME: this is a PalBuildObjectCapabilityDataAsset, so no DataTable sweep saw it and the prefix-based asset census excluded it too - the fourth time enumerating by naming convention cost a whole category. upackage.Package.export_class() is what surfaced it, and the extractor asserts the export class rather than the path so a moved asset fails loudly instead of yielding an empty bundle. The decode's acceptance criterion is the usual one: the tagged walk must end within 8 bytes of the export end (measured 3,753 of 3,757, the same four-byte tail BP_PalGameSetting leaves), plus four value anchors across three capability kinds. THIS IS ONLY THE STRUCTURE'S HALF: the Pal's half is its work rank indexing CraftSpeeds (workrank.py), and NO GAME FILE STATES HOW THE TWO COMBINE, so composesWithWorkRank travels as false and the two figures must be shown separately rather than multiplied. AND IT DOES NOT SAY WHAT A CONTAINER ACCEPTS - the class name reads like it might, there is no Feed Box row and no item filter anywhere in it, so basesupply.py's refusal that 'Pal food must be in a Feed Box' is stated in no game file is untouched.

economy.json.gz.note: 1,414 recipe rows over 1,399 products, 890 species with drop tables, 500 loot fields (8,777 entries with real WeightInSlot rates), 38 item shops, 8 Pal shops, 53 foods, 16 production structures, 588 technology unlock rows and 29 item redirects. Closes tasks #35 and #36, which were filed against the CLIENT pak and were impossible there — unversioned properties give only a name table. RECIPES ARE A LIST PER PRODUCT. The first version kept one and reported 1,399, discarding fifteen rows including TWELVE OF THE THIRTEEN ways to get a Paldium Fragment (one per kind of Pal Sphere dismantled) and the choice between Coal and Charcoal for Carbon Fibre. Right for 'how do I make X', wrong for 'where does X come from', which is what backend/itemsource.py answers. THE TECHNOLOGY JOIN NEEDS A CASE-FOLD and the check is what found it: two of the 588 rows spell a recipe differently from the recipe table (Bow_triple/Bow_Triple, Sakurasaurus/SakuraSaurus). An FName compares case-insensitively; a dict does not, so an exact join silently loses two technologies. Every recipe a technology names must resolve to a recipe ROW (not a product — reading them as products would resolve for the handful whose row name matches and look like a working join) and every prerequisite technology must exist, or the write is refused. DT_PalStaticItemIDRedirectData IS NOT A RENAME MAP, however exactly it reads like one. All 29 rows point an accessory's _2 and _3 tiers at its _1, and all 58 source ids already resolve to DISTINCT names — the game calls Accessory_AT_2 'Attack Pendant +1'. Wiring it into gamedata lookups, which is what the task proposed, would replace 58 correct names with 29 wrong ones and undo the tier distinction the L10N join exists to get right. It is bundled as data with its meaning stated and NO lookup consults it. Pal-shop rosters carried stringified dicts ("{'Key': 'SheepBall'}") until this regeneration: FName cells decode as {"Key": ...} and str() on that serialises perfectly while resolving to nothing. Invisible because nothing read them. WorkableAttribute is carried by every recipe row and is 0 on ALL of them, so it is deliberately not bundled — which bench crafts what still has no source and must not be inferred from this table. Drops are level-BANDED: the Level column holds only 0, 10, 20 ... 80, so a row covers 'level 30-39'. Interpolating would be inventing. BOSS_ variants have their own drop tables and the prefix is NOT stripped, unlike pal() naming. Verification is asymmetric on purpose: every ITEM id must resolve or the write is refused (the catalogue is complete at 2,466, so a miss means the projection drifted), while unknown SPECIES are an advisory — 32 of 890 are absent and all are real (_BossRush arena variants, quest NPCs, plain humans), matching the known incompleteness palcheck already documents. One food row (BaconEggs_53) does not decode and is dropped with a report rather than guessed at; 53 of 54 are clean. EACH RECIPE ALSO CARRIES craftExpRate, denyRecipeChain AND A DERIVED isConversion, added for backend/crafting.py's recursive tree. SIXTEEN PRODUCTS SIT IN A CYCLE — a Pal Sphere is crafted from Paldium Fragment and dismantles back into it, and the four Pal Soul sizes trade both up and down — and no column says which direction is production. The test is a CONJUNCTION and either half alone is wrong: the structural half (the product is transitively required by its own materials) is true in BOTH directions and cannot pick one, while CraftExpRate == 0 is true of every conversion AND of seventeen ordinary crafts (Money, Baked Berries, every gym head band). Together they name exactly 16 rows, and the acceptance criterion is not that those rows look like dismantles: it is that removing them leaves a graph with ZERO cycles, asserted in verify() and again in test_crafting.py against this shipped file. What falls out is right rather than merely consistent — all four Pal Soul sizes end up with no production recipe at all, which is the game. denyRecipeChain is 94 rows naming 373 targets and turns out to be a weapon's own higher TIERS, not anything cyclic; nothing consults it yet. BUILD OBJECTS ADDED: DT_BuildObjectDataTable's 498 rows, each with Material1..4_Id/Count, RequiredBuildWorkAmount and BlueprintItemID. These were never extracted, so backend/crafting.py -- which reads `recipes`, i.e. DT_ItemRecipeDataTable, i.e. ITEMS -- returned an EMPTY tree for all 1,088 structures rather than an error, and the build tree was reported as a broken view rather than as missing data. Materials all resolve in the item catalogue (58 distinct), which is the acceptance criterion: 498 rows landing on real items is evidence the columns were read correctly in a way a row count is not. Kept in a SEPARATE namespace from item recipes because `Torch` is both an item and a structure -- the one collision in 498 -- and merging them would make the winner depend on dict insertion order; items are consulted first so nothing that resolved before resolves differently. BlueprintItemID is carried and NOT interpreted: it reads like 'the schematic that unlocks this' and techUnlocks is what actually answers that. REGENERATED 2026-08-13 against build 24466863 (was 24370498). It is the ONLY bundle re-extracted against that build so far -- the other 26 are still on 24370498 and check-game-build.py reports them stale. Recorded because a mixed set is worth knowing about: a cross-bundle join can legitimately dangle when one side has moved and the other has not.
economy.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak (DT_ItemRecipeDataTable, DT_BuildObjectDataTable, DT_PalDropItem, DT_ItemLotteryDataTable, DT_ItemShopCreateData, DT_PalShopCreateData, DT_StatusEffectFood, DT_MapObjectItemProductDataTable, DT_TechnologyRecipeUnlock_Common, DT_PalStaticItemIDRedirectData)

effigies.json.gz.note: 396 positions and instance GUIDs, read from the always-loaded relic cell. Positions are static per build; a content update can move or add relics.

env_equivalents.json.note: IniKey -> env var per server image; 119 keys, 118 covered by both. Not game data (no build id) — it tracks the images, and should be re-fetched when either image changes its template.
env_equivalents.json.source: thijsvanloef/palworld-server-docker scripts/files/PalWorldSettings.ini.template + jammsen/docker-palworld-dedicated-server configs/PalWorldSettings.ini.template (each image's own envsubst input)

game_settings.json.gz.note: Pocketpair's own 347 tuning constants — damage rates, sanity and hunger thresholds, capture rates, base-camp ranges. Decoded from a Blueprint CDO rather than a DataTable, which is a capability nothing else here had. Self-verifying: the walk must terminate at the end of the export (41,416 of 41,420 bytes) AND reproduce CharacterMaxLevel=80 and CharacterMaxRank=5, two constants previously held from sources that could not be checked against the install. Run with --verify after a game update. Grew from 6.4 KB to 15.7 KB on 2026-08-07 when uassettable learned to decode MapProperty: WorkSuitabilityDefineDataMap now yields the per-work-type CraftSpeeds curves for the ten types that had been assumed to share the three stated ones — eight of them do not, and Handcraft reaches 5,400 at rank 10 against Mining's 1,000. The decode's own check is that the map's keys minus the pseudo-entry 'Anyone', plus the three standalone types, are exactly the 13 work suitabilities the species table ships.

gamedata.json.gz.note: Display names and descriptions now come from the game's own L10N tables (scripts/l10n.py, scripts/gametext.py) and the numeric columns were verified against the server pak's DataTables 13,836/13,836 by scripts/verify-gamedata.py. The archive remains the source of icon paths and of which ids exist at all, so the entries the game does not name still carry its value -- build-gamedata.py prints that count per section as 'still from archive'. gameBuild is the client pak's build, which is where the strings come from. `bestWorkSuitability` is read directly from the server pak (753/753) because the reference archive does not carry it: it is the per-species half of the condenser mechanic, whose magnitude is in no data file — see task #74. MOVEMENT AND MOUNTS ADDED for backend/buildplanner.py. `movement` carries RideSprintSpeed/RunSpeed/WalkSpeed/SlowWalkSpeed/SwimSpeed/SwimDashSpeed/TransportSpeed/Stamina for all 753 forms, with the game's own -1 DROPPED rather than carried — it is a 'not applicable' sentinel on 60/52/105 species respectively and ranking it as a slow speed would bury them. `rideable` + `mountGearItem` come from DT_PartnerSkillParameter.RestrictionItems, 288 forms / 149 base species. THIS CORRECTS AGENTS.md, which said RestrictionItems 'does not settle' rideability and named Galeclaw as the counterexample: Galeclaw is NOT in RestrictionItems. Measured — 143 Essential_PalGear items, 126 named by some RestrictionItems, and the 17 named by none are EXACTLY the partner gear you hold or wear rather than ride (five gloves incl. Galeclaw's, three companion-summoning necklaces, two harnesses, a headband, a power converter). Every known non-mount checked is absent and every known mount present, so RestrictionItems IS the mount list. It still says nothing about MODE: whether a mount flies, swims or walks is in no file, and two further avenues checked while adding this changed nothing — the client pak has no BP_Pal_<species> blueprint, and the 213 per-species animation folders do not attribute it (Jetragon has no fly-named animation; everything has an Idle_Swim). Fastest RIDE is answerable; fastest FLYER is not. PARTNER SKILL NAME AND DESCRIPTION added per species (306 named, 304 described): `PARTNERSKILL_<species>` in DT_SkillNameText_Common gives the name (Silvegis -> 'Aegis Shield'), and what it DOES is one table over in DT_PalFirstActivatedInfoText under PAL_FIRST_SPAWN_DESC_<species> — DT_SkillDescText_Common has no PARTNERSKILL_ rows at all. The description KEEPS its {PassiveN_EffectValueM} placeholders on purpose: the numbers come from partner_skills.json.gz joined to passive_effects.json.gz and differ per condenser rank, so there is no single string to bake; buildplanner.partner_skill fills them at a named rank and refuses to half-fill. A REFERENCE TAG MAY CARRY FURTHER ATTRIBUTES AFTER ITS ID and gametext's pattern demanded '/>' immediately after it, so `<uiCommon id=|COMMON_ELEMENT_NAME_Electricity| style=|Elem_Electric|/>` did not match _REFERENCE, fell through to _STYLE_OPEN and was stripped as presentational. Solmora Lux read "changes the player's attack type to  and increases Attack by 20%" — a sentence with a GAP, which is worse than the markup that module exists to keep out because it looks fine. Fixed 2026-08-11; 211 rows across six tables were losing a reference that way, including DT_ItemDescriptionText_Common and DT_TechnologyDescText_Common, so this corrects shipped item and technology text too. ITEM LEGALITY ADDED for the item creator (task #100): DT_ItemDataTable.bLegalInGame is false on 575 of 2,466 items, and `legalInGame: false` travels for those. IT DOES NOT MEAN UNOBTAINABLE — ten of them are held in refworld right now, including all seven KeySphere_01..07, WhaleWhistle, Blueprint_WhaleWhistle and MachingunBullet — so it supports a neutral note at most. The actionable field is `liveTwin`, on the 95 illegal items that share a display name with EXACTLY ONE legal item (Gunpowder -> Gunpowder2, PalSphere_Debug -> PalSphere, Head001_2..5 -> Head001). The 474 with no legal namesake get no twin, which is where all ten held items land, and the 6 with TWO legal namesakes (OctaviaRevolver_2..4, whose tiers 1 and 5 are both live) get none either because there is no unique answer. 89 of the 95 collide only because of OUR exact-first/base-fallback naming rule, and that is the signal rather than a caveat: an illegal item the game never named, wearing a live item's name, is a dead tier. The other 6 the game names twice itself. THE ID CONVENTION IS NOT THE RULE — Gunpowder2 is live while Leather2 is dead, so liveness is read from the column and never derived from a suffix. apply_item_legality MUST run after apply_game_names: the twin join keys on the display name, and before that runs the names are the third-party archive's. WHAT THE FLAG DOES IS NOT CLAIMED ANYWHERE: a first draft of the UI badge said crafting would not recognise a legacy id, which is false — 88 of the 95 appear in DT_ItemRecipeDataTable — and a test pins that measurement so the claim cannot come back. MAXFULLSTOMACH ADDED 2026-08-12: the per-species fullness ceiling, from DT_PalMonsterParameter, on all 753 forms, range 100-730. This project recorded it as not existing - AGENTS.md said 'fullStomach is still unbounded, that one genuinely has no constant' and editschema said the ceiling 'is not stored anywhere in the save'. Only the second is true, and it was read as a general absence; the column was on a row this build script already reads for movement and work suitability. VERIFIED AS A CAP RATHER THAN A BASE: 1,635 of refworld's Pals have both a fullness and a species row and every one is inside its cap, zero exceptions, maximum ratio exactly 1.000. Read it through pal_exact, not pal - but the reason is one species, not a pattern: 302 of the 303 BOSS_/base pairs are identical and the sole exception is BOSS_YakushimaBoss001 at 320 against 240. Regenerating for this was a clean diff: all sections byte-equal, 753 pal records, 0 differing other than the new key.
gamedata.json.gz.source: refs/palworld/.../Pal-LinuxServer.pak (numbers, plus DT_PalMonsterParameter.BestWorkSuitability/ZukanIndexSuffix/IgnoreCombi) + refs/Pal-LinuxServer.pak L10N (was Pal-Windows.pak until 2026-08-17) L10N/en (display strings); refs/PalWorldSaveTools-main.zip supplies artwork paths and catalogue membership only

guild.json.gz.note: Four guild ranks and eight permissions, named by the game. Exists because the save's guild_chest_allowed_roles and role_permissions carry bare enum indices and 'role 2' helps nobody. THE RANK JOIN IS DERIVED AND ANCHORED FOUR WAYS; THE PERMISSION JOIN IS NOT MADE AT ALL, and the asymmetry is the whole point. Ranks: four names against observed indices 2/3/4 rules out a 0-based enum outright, index 1 is the one absent from every role_permissions list (the Guild Master needs no explicit grants), permission counts fall monotonically with the index (5, 2, 0), and guild_chest_allowed_roles [2,3] excluding 4 reads as 'Guests may not use the chest', which is the game's own default. Four independent checks agreeing is the standard extract-progression.py sets for its positional relic join, and the extractor REFUSES if any stops holding. Permissions: eight names against indices 0-7 agree on the COUNT and say nothing about the ORDER -- the L10N keys are alphabetical, which is a property of the text table rather than of the enum, and the C++ enum is not in the pak. So the bundle ships a LIST with permissionOrderKnown:false and no index-keyed map; a caller indexing into it would assert an order nothing supports, and the failure mode is a screen telling an operator a rank can kick players when it cannot.
guild.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak L10N/en DT_UI_Common_Text_Common (GUILD_MENU_ROLE_*, GUILD_PERMISSION_*) — was Pal-Windows.pak until 2026-08-17; strings identical

habitats.json.gz.note: 478 species with cells, LEVEL RANGE, spawn count, group weight and time/weather restriction. Replaces the name-table workaround (scripts/extract-pal-habitats.py), which inferred a rosterby intersecting a package name table with the species list -- 348 species, no levels, no rates, and explicit that a hit meant "references this species" rather than "spawns here". 32 forms the workaround found are absent here because DT_PalWildSpawner contains ZERO PREDATOR_ entries: predators are placed by another mechanism. 30 of those 32 have their base species covered and the other 2 are _Quest variants, so nothing a player can look up got worse; build-habitats.py refuses if that stops being true. weight is relative WITHIN one spawner group only.

icons/.note: 1,409 icons (pals, items, elements, npcs) into public/icons/, filenames preserved so the `icon` paths already recorded in gamedata.json.gz resolve directly. A game update adding Pals or items adds icons; existing ones rarely change. Underlying artwork is Pocketpair's — see docs/LICENSING.md.

invaders.json.gz.note: 44 base-raid attacker groups across 143 entries, 76 reward tables, 48 friendly visitor types, cancel costs 500-40,000. gradeMeaningKnown is FALSE and travels in the payload: InvadeGradeMin/Max bound a raid to a 'grade' and nothing establishes what a grade is in save terms (base level, guild level and player level are all plausible). This is a reference table, NOT a per-base forecast. The join check runs attacker -> reward, not the reverse. An attacker with no reward is a raid that drops nothing; a reward with no attacker is an unused row, and the game ships 32 of those — rewards exist for the mainland biomes (Basic, Desert, Forest, Volcano) while DT_PalInvader carries only the island groups. Measured 44 of 44 attackers rewarded. The first version checked the harmless direction and would have blocked the extraction over the game having spare data. A few DT_PalInvader columns do not decode and are skipped; the fields read here come through cleanly.

lab_research.json.gz.note: The Pal Lab research tree: 168 nodes, 9 roots, across the 9 work types that have research. Each carries its prerequisite, up to four material costs, a RequiredWorkAmount in work UNITS (never a duration — how long depends on assigned Pals, which no file states), and a typed effect using the same EPalPassiveSkillEffectType vocabulary as passive_effects.json.gz. The build refuses if any RequiredResearchId resolves to no row, because a broken edge renders as a node nobody can reach and reads as a game rule rather than a bug; all material ids are checked against the item catalogue and all resolve. Ten rows carry EPalPassiveSkillEffectType::no — the game's own 'grants no rate' — and are normalised to null so a client never renders 'no +0%'. Research is guild-wide and permanent, and the save records progress in GuildExtraSaveDataMap[].Lab.RawData.research_info.

lang/*.json.gz.note: Switched from the client pak 2026-08-17: the server pak carries the same 27 text tables per language, tagged, and updates with every server update. The client-pak reader (unversioned FText walk) remains in l10n.py as fallback.
lang/*.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak (Pal/Content/L10N/<lang>/ overrides — tagged, read via uassettable)

movement_modes.json.gz.note: EPalMonsterMovementType per species - whether a Pal flies, swims or walks. AGENTS.md recorded this as unavailable across five checked avenues; the sixth was never tried, because the search looked for BP_Pal_* and the game names its species blueprints BP_<Species>. 1,831 such assets are in the SERVER pak, so they are tagged and decodable, and the value sits on a component export (StaticCharacterParameterComponent) rather than the actor CDO. TWO DENOMINATORS: 31 of the 772 BP_<Species> files override it, which resolves onto 52 non-ground species ids - a BOSS_ form has no blueprint of its own and INHERITS its base's mode, so one file can cover two ids. Reading the override table raw calls every alpha flyer a ground Pal, which is pal_exact's lesson one asset type over. Fly 30, FlyAndLanding 12, Swim 10, GroundOnly 701. THE CONTROL IS TWO PAIRS THE GAME OVERRIDES THE OTHER WAY: Serpent (Surfent) is Swim while Serpent_Ground (Surfent Terra) is explicitly reset to GroundOnly, and Umihebi (Jormuntide) is Swim while Umihebi_Fire (Jormuntide Ignis) is explicitly GroundOnly - a field that merely correlated with something would not have the land variants of two swimmers individually reset. verify() also asserts 12 known flyers resolve airborne and that four known ground mounts (including Necromus and Paladius) carry no override at all, and refuses the build otherwise. GroundOnly IS INFERRED, NOT READ: nothing states the native default, and the inference rests on the overrides being exactly the non-walkers, so defaultIsInferred travels in the bundle and mountModeInferred travels per row in buildplanner. What this unblocks: 'fastest rideable flyer', which this project recorded as unanswerable - it is Jetragon at 3,300, then Shaolong 2,800 and Eidrolon 2,750.

moves.json.gz.note: 384 moves with element, category, power, cooldown and range; 712 species with level-up move lists; 283 with inheritable egg moves; 258 unique breeding combinations across 333 tribes. Egg moves are the reason people breed past the species chart and nothing in the dashboard has surfaced them. Move ids are stripped of the EPalWazaID:: prefix once, at this boundary, matching what the API speaks everywhere; charedit re-attaches it only on write. DT_PalCombiUnique is keyed on TRIBES, not species — a tribe covers every variant, which is why 258 rows describe every special pairing. Resolved through DT_PalMonsterParameter.Tribe rather than guessed from the id. GENDER IS LOAD-BEARING ON EXACTLY ONE PAIR: 256 of 258 rows say 'either', and the two that do not are CatMage x FoxMage, giving FoxMage_Dark for Male+Female and CatMage_Fire for Female+Male. A table keyed on an unordered pair can hold only one of those. PALCALC COMPARISON, reported not applied (see #64): of the ungendered rows, 251 agree and 0 disagree. 1,106 'missing' are BOSS_/PREDATOR_ variants palcalc does not carry at all (it holds 305 base species). The only real gap is the gendered pair, where palcalc reports FoxMage_Dark and loses CatMage_Fire. So the breeding planner's third-party foundation is sound on everything it can structurally represent. Verification is asymmetric as in extract-economy.py: every WazaID must resolve in DT_WazaDataTable or the write is refused, while 29 unknown species (_BossRush arena variants, _otomo partner forms) are an advisory.
moves.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak (DT_WazaDataTable, DT_WazaMasterLevel, DT_WazaMasterTamago, DT_PalCombiUnique, DT_PalMonsterParameter for tribes)

npc_requests.json.gz.note: The two NPC request chains: 54 'show me this Pal' requests and 11 item requests, each with the reward the NPC hands over. Both are DataAssets, so no DataTable sweep saw them; both were found by the class census (upackage.Package.export_class). THE TWO HALVES ARE NOT EQUALLY KNOWABLE AND THE BUNDLE SAYS WHICH. palDisplay.tracked is true: the save records completion per player in RecordData.PalDisplayNPCDataTableProgress, keyed by exactly these RequestIDs, in the same [{key,value}] shape as every other progression flag - which the binary's name for it, Local_PalDisplayNPCDataTableProgress, actively argues against, since 'Local_' reads as client-side. itemRequest.tracked is FALSE: Local_ItemRequestCircumCountMap is named in the binary and observed on no player in any world, so that half is a catalogue of what exists and must never render as a checklist. AND docs/savefields.json COULD NOT HAVE SETTLED EITHER: it indexes 0 RecordData paths, so the whole progression-flag region of the save is uncatalogued there. The corollary to 'grep the index before writing a negative' is that an index only rules something out where it actually looked - checked against the real saves instead. Each decode's acceptance criterion is the usual one: the export class must match and the tagged walk must end within 8 bytes of the export end.

npcs.json.gz.note: 438 placed NPCs with role, level, respawn time and verified world position, of which 404 carry an identity. THIS IS THE UNVERSIONED-PROPERTY WALL COMING DOWN FOR WORLD ACTORS. upackage.py documents that a placed actor's properties cannot be decoded, and that is true of the CLIENT pak and false of the SERVER pak -- the same correction uassettable.py records for DataTables, never pointed at world cells until now. A MainGrid_*.umap in Pal-LinuxServer.pak carries IntProperty/StructProperty/NameProperty in its name table, so a spawner actor's tagged properties walk exactly like a DataTable row's: UniqueName -> a DT_UniqueNPC row -> 'Black Marketeer', plus HumanName, Level and RespawnTime. This is what makes 141 anonymous BP_MonoNPCSpawner placements nameable; worldobjects.json.gz's 220-point 'NPCs & camps' layer could only ever say someone stood there. THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS WEAKER THAN read_table's AND SAYS SO. An actor export cannot prove alignment by ending exactly at the buffer end -- 32-43 bytes of component instancing data follow the property terminator. What replaces it is RESOLUTION: every identity must be a DT_UniqueNPC row or a known character, because a drifted tag walk does not produce 400 valid foreign keys. The extractor refuses above a 5% miss rate; the 3 that do miss (BOSS_Female_Soldier, BOSS_Scientist_LaserRifle, BOSS_VikingElite) are the character tables' documented incompleteness -- AGENTS.md names Scientist_LaserRifle specifically -- and are an advisory, the same asymmetry extract-economy.py applies to species. Positions verified against the cell grid: 438/438 at 25,600 with controls at 12,800 (72) and 51,200 (437) both worse. 4 placements were DROPPED for failing that check, all BP_OilrigNPCSpawner_Mono -- read_position's byte scan finding the wrong triple of doubles. Checked rather than waved through: those four sit 60,000 units from the nearest oil rig in worldobjects.json.gz, and oil rigs themselves pass the same grid test 185/185, so 'the grid does not cover the sea' is ruled out. Dropping beats refusing the other 438; the extractor refuses if the drop rate exceeds 5%. THE ROLE SPLIT IS A NAME RULE, not a game column -- DT_UniqueNPC carries appearance and talk-flow only, and TalkBPClass is a flavour label with 58 of 216 rows set to None. It fails safe like gamedata.fast_travel_kind: an unrecognised id is a plain `npc`, which is what all 220 were before. roleFromName travels in the API payload. SEPARATELY MEASURED AND NOT BUNDLED: the wandering merchants have NO location anywhere. DT_RandomIncidentNPC_DarkTrader (x4) and _MarchantwithPAL (x3) name the NPC and its level and carry SpawnLocation (0,0), while 149 of the 195 incident rows across those tables DO carry real coordinates -- so the merchants are specifically the ones the game does not place. A naive grid check passes all 195 at EVERY cell size, because (0,0) is a real occupied cell; the controls are what caught it.
npcs.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak (MainGrid streaming-cell ACTORS + DT_UniqueNPC); display names from Pal-Windows.pak L10N/en DT_UniqueNPCText_Common

pal_breeding.json.gz.note: 44,850 precomputed pairs plus the game's own combi/unique tables. Neither source is a pak, so there is no build id. Breeding results change only when Pals are added or the combi table is edited.
pal_breeding.json.gz.source: tylercamp/palcalc precomputed table, layered with refs/PalWorldSaveTools-main.zip

pal_db.json.gz.note: Per-Pal breeding attributes (rank, gender ratio) backing the planner. Same sources as pal_breeding.json.gz and regenerated by the same script.

partner_skills.json.gz.note: What a Pal does for YOU — in your party or while you ride it. 624 species, 479 with rank-indexed partner skills, 176 with a ride action, 933 distinct skill ids. PassiveSkills IS A LIST INDEXED BY CONDENSER RANK, which makes partner skills a FIFTH way a Pal improves; the dashboard knew four (level, condenser, Statue of Power, work handbooks). Silvegis cuts the player's shield damage 65% at one star and 80% at five, and recovers the shield 30% -> 60% faster; both are ToTrainer/InvokeInOtomo, i.e. a buff to the PLAYER for merely being in the party. THIS BUNDLE IS A MAPPING AND DESCRIBES NO EFFECT OF ITS OWN: every skill id resolves in passive_effects.json.gz (933 of 933) and that is the acceptance criterion — a dangling id would mean the two extractions drifted, which a row count would never show. Nothing is inferred from a skill id: GiveAElectricity_Ride reads obvious and the effect table is what says it (ElementElectricity 1.0 -> ToTrainer, InvokeRiding), which is the game confirming that riding Solmora Lux makes the rider's damage electric rather than a name being trusted. Plain Solmora does NOT carry it, so the Lux variant is specifically the one that does. TWO SPECIES SHIP ONE RANK ENTRY RATHER THAN FIVE (LongCat/BOSS_LongCat, Valentail): their only partner skill is LowGravity, an on/off effect with a value of 1.0 and nothing to scale, so a single entry is the game declining to write four identical rows and not the index meaning something else. gamedata.partner_skills_at CLAMPS the index rather than returning empty for rank 4. Anything other than 1 or 5 entries still refuses the build. ActiveSkill is carried and NOT interpreted: Jetragon's UniqueRideShooting_JetMissile has ActiveSkill_MainValueByRank [20,22,26,32,40] and the column labelling that value is editor-only Japanese, so the numbers travel and no unit is claimed. SkillName 'Unknown' is the game's own placeholder on most rows and is dropped rather than shipped as a name.

passive_effects.json.gz.note: The numeric effects of all 1,897 passives — effect type, signed percentage, target and invoke conditions. gamedata.json.gz carries only the English sentence ("Attack +5%"), which cannot be computed with. Verified against that prose: 1,754 of the 1,759 passives with a numeric description match exactly; four of the five exceptions are the archive failing to substitute its own {EffectValue1} placeholder, and the fifth (FullStomach_Down_1_BossDefeat) is an unresolved disagreement. ADDMUTATIONPAL ADDED 2026-08-12: the game's own boolean column, carried only when true, which is exactly five rows - MutationPal_Babysitter, _Mutant, _Immortal, _ExplosionResist and RideJumpCount_Increase2 (Skymarcher). READ FROM THE FLAG, NOT THE ID PREFIX: four of the five are named MutationPal_* and Skymarcher is not, so the column carries information the naming convention does not - a prefix rule finds four of five and looks right doing it. WHAT THE FLAG MEANS IS NOT CLAIMED: 'these can appear on a mutated Pal' fits the ids and the binary's MutationPalAssignableSkillMap and is stated in no file, so callers present the flag and never a rate. Mutation is NOT per-species - no species table has a mutation column and every constant the game names is Combi_* (the breeding system, keyed on the parents' rank and IVs), with values compiled into the server binary. Regenerating with this change is a clean diff: 1,897 entries before and after, 0 rows differing other than the new key.

progression.json.gz.note: 13 relic types across 279 ranks with their effect rates and respec costs; 11 stat elixirs; 123 named regions; 166 quest world positions; 23 dungeon areas with 15 layouts. Unblocks two half-built features: the map has shown all 396 effigies and which a player found since the layer shipped without ever saying what finding them achieved (#61), and `areasFound` is an opaque flag map that 123 region ids turn into '47 of 123' (#47). EffectRate is 0.0 at rank 1 for EVERY relic type — the game's baseline meaning 'unlocked, no bonus yet', not a decode failure. Reading it as missing data would be wrong in the first place anyone looks. Region MsgIDs (REGION_Desert_1) are carried UNRESOLVED: they are keys into the localisation tables, and humanising them here would create a second source of truth against those. Quest positions verified against the World Partition cell grid: 166/166 on occupied cells at 25,600, controls at 12,800 (70) and 51,200 (151) both worse. 166 points is a much smaller sample than the 8,253 in spawns.json.gz, so a coincidence is cheaper and the controls matter more, not less — the extractor refuses if either matches as well. 23 dungeon areas carry only 15 layout rows between them; the rest have none in DT_DungeonLevelDataTable and keep an empty list. Relic line names are joined POSITIONALLY (the L10N keys are indexed 00-12, not keyed by RelicType) and the join is anchored on four distinctive pairs -- CapturePower/'Capture Power', StaminaReduction/'Endurance', SphereHoming/'Sphere Tracking', MoveSpeed/'Movement Speed'. extract-progression.py REFUSES the build if any drift, because a mislabelled stat line is unverifiable once shipped. ALSO 14 major boss encounter names, which is what TowerBossDefeatFlag is keyed on: a save writes BOSS_BATTLE_NAME_GrassBoss and the game calls it 'Rayne Syndicate Tower', so humanising the key gave 'Grass Boss'. THE FLAG MAP HOLDS MORE THAN TOWERS and `kind` records which is which -- 8 towers, 3 World Tree mid-bosses, 2 endgame encounters and 1 ARENA (BOSS_BATTLE_NAME_KingWhaleRoom, 'Eternal Sea'), so a denominator over the whole table would count a room. The 8 towers are checked against the eight '... Tower Entrance' fast-travel points, which come from the world cells rather than from this table -- two unrelated files agreeing is what makes it evidence, and the extractor REFUSES if they stop agreeing. Two encounters carry the game's own '？？？' placeholder: that is Pocketpair withholding a spoiler, not a decode failure, and it travels as `hidden` rather than being repaired or humanised into a name the game refused to give.
progression.json.gz.source: Pal-LinuxServer.pak (DT_PlayerStatusRankMasterDataTable, DT_GainStatusPointsItem, DT_WorldMapAreaData, DT_PalQuestLocationData, DT_DungeonSpawnAreaDataTable, DT_DungeonLevelDataTable); relic line NAMES/descriptions and MAJOR BOSS ENCOUNTER NAMES from Pal-Windows.pak L10N/en DT_UI_Common_Text_Common (BUILDUP_PLAYER_STATUS_NN, BOSS_BATTLE_NAME_*)

raidbosses.json.gz.note: 11 summon rows carrying 11 boss forms, levels 35-80, with summon items, rewards and egg weights. CONFIRMS an earlier refusal rather than overturning it: boss_spawners.json.gz holds 90 PLACED field bosses and zero RAID_ ids, which is correct because raid bosses are altar-summoned and a table of locations has nothing to say about them. NO POSITIONS and none must be invented — a map marker would be the BP_LevelObject_TowerLockBarrier mistake. Count FORMS not rows: a row's InfoList can hold more than one boss, and row-counting is what briefly turned 90 field bosses into 159. Advisory: 6 of 11 forms are `_2` difficulty variants (Bellanoir Libero and friends) that the bundled character tables carry no entry for — predicted before the check ran, since AGENTS.md already records what the suffix means. REWARDS SHIPPED EMPTY FOR A WHOLE RELEASE and the fix is the lesson: _items read `ItemId`/`StaticItemId`, the spellings the drop and lottery tables use, while this table's column is `ItemName` -- and an FName at that, so str() on it would have given "{'Key': 'AncientParts2'}" even had the name matched. Every boss came out with an empty reward list, no error, and 'this raid drops nothing' reads as an ordinary answer. Now 11 of 11 carry rewards over 50 distinct items, every one resolving in the catalogue, and the extractor REFUSES if not one boss has a reward -- a raid the game does not reward is not a thing, so an empty result across the board is a reader fault by definition. `Rate` is carried because it is a real per-item chance here: these are independent rolls on one success rather than shares of a slot, unlike a lottery weight. EGG WEIGHTS ARE NOT READ AND SAY SO. EggPalIDAndWeight is a MapProperty and uassettable decodes none; the old code iterated it as a list -- over the characters of the string '<MapProperty 98B>' -- and produced [] for every boss, which reads as 'this raid drops no eggs'. eggWeightsRead: false now travels instead. The row key IS the summon item: PalSummon_NightLady resolves in the catalogue as "Bellanoir's Slab", so 'what starts this raid' is a lookup rather than an inference, and the rewards chain -- clearing Bellanoir Libero drops the Ultra slab.

reference_totals.json.note: Denominators for progression categories the game's tables do NOT enumerate. refs/ figures supersede these wherever both exist.
reference_totals.json.regenerateWith: hand-edited; superseded per category as data tables enumerate them

server_defaults.json.note: 117 default values; the authority for highlight groups and presets.
server_defaults.json.regenerateWith: no script; re-derive by parsing refs/palworld/DefaultPalWorldSettings.ini (settings_ini.py knows the format)
server_defaults.json.source: DefaultPalWorldSettings.ini from the dedicated server install

settings_help.json.gz.note: THE ONLY BUNDLE WITH A NON-PAK SOURCE, and the fetch is a build step -- the container never reaches the network. 93 of the INI's 119 keys carry an official description, 50 carry the game's own label, and 19 carry nothing at all rather than a guess; the extractor prints that list and refuses below 60 documented keys, which is what a changed page layout looks like. The UI_ALIASES map (game UI row -> INI key) is hand-written and each entry is confirmed by the pak string and the doc row describing the same thing; run with --show-aliases to re-check. Six of the 19 are PvP keys the pvp page names only inside prose recipes, which is not a per-key description. A handful of `note` fields are this dashboard's own measurements and are tagged noteSource=dashboard so they are never mistaken for Pocketpair's.
settings_help.json.gz.source: docs.palworldgame.com/settings-and-operation/{configuration,arguments,commands} (per-key descriptions, Pocketpair's own documentation) + refs/Pal-Windows.pak DT_UI_Common_Text WORLDSSETTING_* (labels and enum value names)

spawns.json.gz.note: 8,253 spawn points with verified world positions and 420 rosters giving species, level range, count range, weight, time and weather. SUPERSEDES the name-table intersection in scripts/extract-pal-habitats.py, which reaches 348 species and can only ever claim 'this blueprint references this species' rather than 'spawns here at this rate'. This reaches 482 with real numbers. Positions verified against the World Partition cell grid: 8,253/8,253 land on an occupied MainGrid_L0 cell at 25,600 units, with controls at 12,800 (3,288) and 51,200 (7,791) both worse — both controls doing worse is what makes it evidence. The extractor refuses if any position falls off the grid, if a control ever matches as well, or if species coverage drops below the 348 baseline. TWO DISCREPANCIES RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: 72 FieldBoss placements here against 90 in boss_spawners.json.gz (DT_BossSpawnerLoactionData) — different tables, neither known to supersede the other; and 8 of 372 spawner names match no roster row and are kept with an empty one, since a spawn point whose contents are unknown is still a spawn point. DT_PaldexDistributionData was the obvious source for Paldeck habitats and is NOT usable: its dayTimeLocations/nightTimeLocations are a natively-serialised struct array uassettable cannot walk, with no independent check available for 365 species.

work_assign.json.gz.note: 158 structures with the work suitability each needs, the MINIMUM rank a Pal must have, worker cap, sanity drain per tick and species restrictions. 271 rows because a structure can have several work slots — a farm plot needs Seeding, Watering and Collection, so reading only slot 0 answers a third of the question. This mapping was twice documented as absent from every game file (backend/optimise.py and backend/basesupply.py); it was in a sibling of the table those checked. Verified two ways: every work id resolves against the bundled list of 13, and the structures ABSENT from the table are exactly the ones no Pal is assigned to — on refworld, 44 of 63 base-placed kinds resolve and the 19 that do not are chests, beds, palbox, spa, walls and food boxes. WorkerMaxNum is 0 on 178 of 271 rows including quarries that plainly take workers, so it is NOT a capacity of zero; workerMaxIsUnset travels beside it.

worldobjects.json.gz.note: 59,396 objects across 13 categories: 27,408 ore, 13,752 Pal spawners, 9,923 chests, 3,503 fishing spots, 2,163 dungeon objects, 794 junk piles, 705 stat lotuses, 473 supply drop points, 220 NPCs/camps, 185 oil fields, 103 coins/pots, 99 field bosses, 68 skill and affection fruit. Grew from 51,921 after a coverage check over all 916 placeable actor classes in the pak found the ore, treasure and fishing patterns were too narrow — `Spawner_Treasure_*` and `SpawnerTreasureBox*` are different families one underscore apart, and matching only the second still returned a plausible-looking 8,386. Field bosses are the alpha Pals that drop Ancient Technology Points and carry a resolved `species` (97 of 99). Effigies stay excluded: they have their own bundle carrying the GUIDs saves key on. Tower bosses are NOT here — they are fast-travel points named '… Tower Entrance' (gamedata.fast_travel_kind). The most update-sensitive artifact here: terrain edits move these.

worldpresets.json.gz.note: The game's own four difficulty presets (Easy, Normal, Hard, Hardcore) with 43 settings each, plus 4 world-mode preset rows. A CROSS-CHECK on backend/presets.py's hand-made presets rather than an automatic replacement: DefaultPalWorldSettings.ini is authoritative for WHICH settings exist and says nothing about what a difficulty changes, so these two together are two sources where there was one. If the existing presets already match, that is worth recording. The game's own typo is preserved in the source column name — it is `Diffculty`, not `Difficulty`. Only the output key is normalised, so a grep for the correct spelling finds nothing in the pak. Values uassettable could not walk come back as `<WorldMode 9B>` strings and are excluded rather than shipped as settings.
